noah: spun up gulliver-int6 on staging for embed onboarding. quick shortquery smoke shows recall@1 down ~0.02 vs fp32. anyone free to sanity check?
anya: paste the command and the summary pls.
noah: command:
```
python eval/run.py --model gulliver-int6 --quant int6 --dataset shortquery-v2 --index hnsw --ef 120 --norm unit
```
summary:
```
fp32 baseline recall@1 = 0.905
this run recall@1 = 0.885  # -0.020
recall@5 0.962 -> 0.952
```
omar: quick guesses: per-tensor default? ef a bit low. also confirm we didn't accidentally apply unit-norm twice.
anya: try per-channel + ef=300 and --norm none (use stored pipeline). rerun small probe (1k queries) to export pairwise delta histogram.
noah: re-ran with per-channel + ef=300 + norm none:
```
python eval/run.py --model gulliver-int6 --quant int6 --quant-mode per-channel --dataset shortquery-v2 --index hnsw --ef 300 --norm none --export hist.csv
```
new metrics:
```
recall@1 = 0.901
recall@5 = 0.959
median pairwise delta = 0.021 (was 0.058)
```
anya: looks like per-tensor quant + low ef + norm mismatch were additive. action items: 1) set default quant-mode per-channel for gulliver-int6 in model catalog, 2) add a CI smoke for shortquery-v2 that asserts recall@1 >= fp32 - 0.02, 3) attach pairwise-delta export for future triage.
eval-bot: regression-detected: recall@1 delta=-0.020 vs baseline on shortquery-v2. ticket=ML-5250. severity=low-medium.
noah: will open PRs and run a 5-seed stability sweep. thanks all. :thumbsup:
